creativity.reason: Level 1: the business is a multi-asset exchange with no creative product line; the only creative activity is incidental volunteer craft workshops, and when torn between 1 and 2 the lower level was chosen.

community.reason: Level 3: named external education (SGX Academy, over 170 events and more than 22,000 participants) and a named community-investment programme (Bull Charge, more than $52 million raised) show substantial measured reach, but neither is central to strategy.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: the exchange serves listing companies and issuers, but describes no current, specific programme aimed at barriers for founders or small businesses; the emerging-companies initiative (E10) is planned only.

notes: SGX Academy investor education sits close to the 'educating customers' trap, because the exchange benefits from new investors. It is counted because the report frames it under CSR financial literacy, partners with tertiary institutions and targets young first-time investors. Community 3 also rests independently on Bull Charge. Several figures are split by PDF layout callouts and could not be quoted as continuous text: $2.25 million raised in 2024, about 4,500 Charity Run participants, and over 2,800 volunteer hours across 33 activities. The Sports Fun Workshops for people on the autism spectrum were also split this way. The report points to a separate FY2025 Sustainability Report for fuller detail, but the annual report itself describes specific activities, so coverage is sufficient. The chairman's letter discusses startups and venture capital as policy commentary only. Catalist is mentioned only as a 2007 milestone. Workforce gender, age and geographic splits are disclosed but count as demographics only.
